## 1. What the lane claims

Reviewed HEAD `b96b73315edb21bc54763bfd2b500314610935d0`, against fetched integration `927436b8c463c25e3c85e1608da087aa5c3d7a89`. Read CLAUDE.md, lane-review/SKILL.md, LESSONS.md lines 1–40, HANDOFF §§0/P3, the brief, and REPORT_165.md. No lane source/record edits or checkout/index/commit changes were made. The specifically requested `git fetch origin` succeeded silently. Three rev165 probes already existed before this review; I inspected and reran them, and added only `probes/rev165_fidelity.lean`, `probes/rev165_audit_note.lean`, and this report.

The lane claims the order-half velocity embedding, not the entire draft A05 API: `REPORT_165.md:35`, `:157`; `COMPARISON.md:220`. Its final statement, in `formalization/NSFormalization/Section4/A05/CriticalL3.lean:394`, is exactly

```lean
∀ z : NSFormalization.Section4.A02.SpatialField,
  NSFormalization.Section4.A02.MemHInfty z →
  eLpNorm z 3 volume ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal criticalL3Const * dotHomogeneousENorm (1 / 2) z
```

`criticalL3Const = 3 * scalarCriticalConst (1/2)`, with `scalarCriticalConst a = coefficient a * (potentialConstant a * 512 ^ (1 / targetExponent a))` (`CriticalL3.lean:166`, `:302`). Constants are fixed before the field, universally positive in the stated range, and do not depend on a chosen datum.

Paper fidelity: opened `paper/sections/04-whole-space.tex:81–112` and `paper/sections/appendix-b-embeddings.tex:11–73` with sed. The exact velocity inequality is at whole-space line 93 / appendix line 29; the brief's lines 105–112 are its continuation application (line 109 uses the velocity L³ bound). Appendix lines 22–24 authorize componentwise constants, and lines 26–27 restrict to finite homogeneous norms. The totalized ENNReal inequality agrees with that finite case. It does not purport to prove the PDE estimate or full continuation result.

### Lead checkpoint 1 — canonical norm: rfl

Fetched/read `origin/erenup/164-D01-g1-homogeneous-norm` at `18b6508df2983f9fe66730e5b724a9b733db7f9b`, using git show. Its `formalization/NSFormalization/Section4/D01/HomogeneousNorm.lean:26–27` and lane 165 `CriticalL3.lean:49–50` have the identical infimum body:

```lean
⨅ G : {G : RealVectorSobolev s // IsHomogeneousSliceDatum s z G}, ‖G.1‖ₑ
```

Only the written type qualification differs (`Homogeneous.SpatialField` versus opened `SpatialField`), resolving to the same declaration. Both predicates resolve to `D01.Homogeneous.IsHomogeneousSliceDatum` (`HomogeneousWitness.lean:251`), with the same component predicate (:235), real-vector subtype, and enorm. Thus `A05.dotHomogeneousENorm = D01.dotHomogeneousENorm` will be `rfl`, not an analytic lemma. The local transcription probe checks exactly this equality (`probes/rev165_nonvacuity.lean:16–21`). Lane 164's `verification/Contracts/V1/HomogeneousNorm.lean:31–32` instead opens the frozen Data predicate; its unfolded body is also definitionally equal. A second rfl probe against that exact contract body passes (`probes/rev165_fidelity.lean:13–18`). No canonical module was installed into this worktree.

### Lead checkpoint 2 — hypotheses: exact match

`research/A05/Spec.lean:366–368` asks for `∀ v : SpatialField, MemHInfty v → ...`; it does not ask for initialClassR or a solution object. The spec opens frozen Data; A02's restatement (`A02/SolutionClass.lean:88`) is definitionally identical, verified by rfl in `probes/rev165_fidelity.lean:9`. Therefore the lane hypothesis is neither weaker nor stronger than the spec. It is weaker than membership in initialClassR, which additionally requires solenoidality (`SolutionClass.lean:97`).

For a ClassicalSolutionR slice at `t ∈ Ico 0 T`, spatial smoothness comes from `w.velocity_smooth` and `D01.contDiff_slice` (`SolutionClass.lean:121`, `D01/DatumToJets.lean:366`); the datum half of MemHInfty comes from `w.sobolev` (`SolutionClass.lean:133`). The complete application is checked in `probes/rev165_fidelity.lean:19–28`. This covers the intended R43/R44 velocity consumers; `w.sobolev` alone supplies the datum conjunct, not smoothness.

### Lead checkpoint 3 — non-vacuity and smallness

No-datum branch: `CriticalL3.lean:398–409` explicitly uses empty infimum = top and strictly positive finite constant times top = top. Datum branch: line 401 rewrites the norm to `‖G‖ₑ`, which is finite for an element of the normed datum space, and line 402 invokes the proved finite estimate. No `top.toReal = 0` shortcut occurs.

The worker's bump is genuinely nonzero and smooth compactly supported, but its displayed nonvac theorem (`axioms_critical_l3.lean:52`) does not itself assert finite homogeneous norm. I independently reran the strengthened bump probe: `probes/rev165_nonvacuity.lean:41–57` obtains a half-order datum using `D01.Homogeneous.isHomogeneousSliceDatum_compact` (`D01/HomogeneousWitness.lean:517`) and proves both the homogeneous norm and L³ norm are not top. Its final example at line 71 packages nonzeroness, datum existence and both finiteness conclusions. Thus this is a real finite-norm instance, not merely an invocation in the top branch.

The paper smallness hypothesis (`04-whole-space.tex:85`) is a finite real threshold. Its faithful ENNReal form (`research/R43/Spec.lean:215–216`) forces the initial homogeneous norm to be finite and hence its datum type to be inhabited. This implication is proved in `probes/rev165_nonvacuity.lean:58–69`. No extra `≠ top` assumption is missing from the final embedding or initial smallness condition. Finiteness/continuity for later slices still belongs to the downstream homogeneous-constructor/path work; initial smallness alone is not a proof of every later slice's finiteness.

### Lead checkpoint 4 — constants and normalization

`Source/RieszKernelNormalization.lean:11–18`: coefficient is `Gamma((3-a)/2)/(2^a * π^(3/2) * Gamma(a/2))`; both Gamma arguments and all denominator factors are positive for `0<a<3/2`, as certified by coefficient_pos (which even permits a<3).

`Source/RieszPotentialLp.lean:14–20`: targetExponent is `6/(3-2*a)` and potentialConstant is `4*π/a + sqrt(4*π/(3-2*a))`. The first summand is strictly positive; the square root is nonnegative (indeed positive in range). `512^(1/targetExponent a)` is a positive real power of a strictly positive real base; at a=1/2 the exponent is 1/3. None is an ENNReal.toReal of a possibly infinite quantity. `CriticalL3.lean:171–175` and :305 certify the products' positivity.

The normalization is not silently dropped: `Source/RieszKernelNormalization.lean:21` has coefficient × kernel constant = `(2π)^(-a)`; `Source/RieszSingularMultiplier.lean:76,85` uses that factor; `Source/RieszL2Fourier.lean:61` proves the normalized commuting square. `CriticalL3.lean:90–153` converts angular data correctly, and :256 uses that square. Opened `Source/FractionalRealization.lean:78,96`, `Source/RieszPotentialOperator.lean:97`, and `Paper1/SchwartzCriticalEmbedding.lean:57,171`: they are the advertised completion/Schwartz analytic route. The new proof directly uses the underlying potentialOperator bound and normalized square, rather than literally applying FractionalRealization.realization_norm_le_datum.

The API names have no declaration matches (only CriticalL3's homogeneousLeSobolev docstring). Semantic candidates were also opened: `Source/BesselFractionalData.lean:45,55,86` supplies scalar contraction and cancellation but not the complete angular physical vector constructor; `D01/HomogeneousWitness.lean:517` supplies compact-smooth data (including endpoint orders), not all MemHInfty fields; `B02/LebesgueDatum.lean:345` has s≤0; `Paper3/SobolevOrderLowering.lean:26,39,78` is inhomogeneous lowering, not the complete Bessel-power physical relation.
